subject: Fleet runway sync: proposal for deal-linked reserved slots + contingency
messages:
From: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: Tim Huang <tim.huang@quasar-analytics.com>, Maya Patel <maya.patel@quasar-analytics.com>
Date: 2027-12-12T08:03:00-08:00
Subject: Fleet runway sync: proposal for deal-linked reserved slots + contingency

Team —

Following our pipeline review, Quasar has moved from pilot to a near-term expansion ask. They are requesting reserved capacity in H1 to support steady inference for a new analytics feature. I sketched a proposal and two contingency scenarios attached (spreadsheet + one-pager). High level:

- Ask: 12 dedicated slots starting Feb 1 for six months (steady throughput, low percentiles SLO)
- Contingency A: start with 8 reserved + 2 burstable slots, commit to scale if usage ramps
- Contingency B: deferred reserve with routing to burst capacity and strict prefix caching to control cost

Please review the attached matrix and confirm stove-piping constraints from infra and finance. Key questions:
1) Can infra provision 12 units by Feb 1 if we approve today? (Ben)
2) What is the finance view on a 6-month reserved commitment at the proposed discount? (Laura)
3) Any model/quantization changes that materially change slot sizing assumptions? (Karthik)

Tim/Maya — looped you in so you're aware of the ask; I'm copying the forecast tab from your export to ensure we're aligned. We need a quick decision window this week to lock pricing and capacity.

Action: please reply with "PROVISION" / "LIMITED" / "DELAY" + any blockers.

Thanks,
Grace
Grace O'Connor
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
Attachments: QSR-9742_pipeline_forecast_Q4.xlsx (spreadsheet), reserve_scenarios_matrix_v2.pdf (summary PDF)

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-12-12T09:18:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Fleet runway sync: proposal for deal-linked reserved slots + contingency

+1 on the ask — infrastructure feasibility notes below.

Short answer: provisionable but with caveats.

- We currently have a 3-week lead on procurement for the specific A100-like SKU Quasar's stack needs. If we decide today, slice scheduling + allocation can complete by 2028-02-01 with a finger in the wind.
- Operationalizing 12 dedicated slots requires a small config change to our autoscaler to pin the pool to Quasar's CID for isolation. I can get an engineer on it but need approval for a change freeze window (patch scheduled next Tue).
- Burstable slots (Contingency A) are straightforward and would be the path of least resistance to meet Feb latency targets; they do increase preemption risk.

Blockers:
- Budget sign-off for the reserved commitment (Laura)
- Final list of model variants and inference profile from the customer (Karthik)

I'll hold tentative provisioning work until I hear "PROVISION" from finance / sales.

-ben
Ben Carter
Head of Fleet Ops

From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-12-12T11:32:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Fleet runway sync: proposal for deal-linked reserved slots + contingency

Thanks — fiscal constraints noted. Finance position: we can approve a 6-month commitment at 8 reserved slots at 18% discount; the 12-slot ask would need a stretched commit (12 months) or a higher discount to get to your numbers.

- Proposal: accept Contingency A (8 reserved + 2 burstable) with an option to convert to full 12 reserved after 90 days if consumption reaches 75% of committed throughput. This protects cash while giving Quasar runway.
- Require: signed SOW with explicit conversion clause and a DocuSign path (link below) before provisioning work starts.

If sales agrees, I'll route contract amendment + finance approval by EOD Friday.

-Laura
Laura Bennett
Director, Revenue Operations

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-12-12T14:07:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Fleet runway sync: proposal for deal-linked reserved slots + contingency

Quick tech check from model side:

- The model Quasar will serve (q-analytics-v3) in float16 consumes ~0.85x the slot baseline we use for our standard estimate — so 12 slots in our spreadsheet look conservative. Quantization to int8 could drop effective CPU/GPU memory footprint further but would add a ~3–5% latency variance we should flag to the customer.
- If we agree to Contingency A, we can recommend an initial quantization trial in staging to validate tail-latency. If trial looks good, conversion to the full reserved commitment should be lower risk.

No infra blockers on my end; will provide a short performance runbook for the CS/release engineers by Thursday.

-Karthik
Applied ML — Inference Optimizations

From: Tim Huang <tim.huang@quasar-analytics.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>
Cc: Maya Patel <maya.patel@quasar-analytics.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-12-13T16:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Fleet runway sync: proposal for deal-linked reserved slots + contingency

Grace — thanks for looping us in and for the clear scenarios. Quasar is comfortable starting with Contingency A (8 reserved + 2 burstable) and the 90-day conversion trigger sounds fair. Two quick asks from our side:

1) Can Redwood guarantee no more than 2 full restarts (hard preemptions) per month on the burstable slots? We rely on small job affinity for downstream scheduling.
2) We need the conversion clause in the SOW to explicitly reference the usage telemetry that will be used (token throughput, p95 latency). Can you work with Laura to get the language in the DocuSign template?

We'll sign the amendment once those two items are in — target to return signed DocuSign by Friday.

Best,
Tim Huang
Head of Platform Engineering, Quasar Analytics
